messages:
alyssa: Heads up — onboarding sample app caused duplicate completions during a demo. Client retried after a 429 and the server processed the original a bit later, so we ended up with two side effects. Suspect idempotency key TTL + clock skew issue.

jamie: Oof. Which SDK/version and how are you generating the idempotency key/TTL?

alyssa: Node SDK v0.8.2. We generate a UUID client-side and attach X-Idempotency-Token + X-Idempotency-TTL=10s. Server seems to honor a 5s dedupe window. If client clock is ahead the token can already be out of window when server checks.

marta: That sounds like a classic skew + client-ttl mismatch. Relying solely on client TTL is fragile.

paul: Quick options: (1) sample app switches to server-backed idempotency token flow (create token, then call), (2) SDK applies server Date header to compute skew and adjust TTLs, or (3) server tolerates a small grace window.

jamie: SDK could auto-calc skew on first response: store offset = server_date - local_date and apply to future TTL math. Also add jitter to retries so everyone doesn't hammer at the same instant.

alyssa: Confirmed repro involves token refresh race + multi-region routing: token issued in region A, request routed to B, original processed late. Client retried immediately (no jitter) so duplicate happened.

marta: Suggest we implement three safeguards: 1) skew-aware TTL, 2) jittered exponential backoff on retry by default, 3) demo/sample app uses server-issued idempotency token or exposes easy helper that does that.

jamie: Proposed snippet for skew-adjusted TTL + backoff: 
```
const skew = new Date(serverDate).getTime() - Date.now();
const adjustedTTL = Math.max(1, clientTTL + Math.floor(skew / 1000));
const backoff = baseDelay * Math.pow(2, attempt) * (1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * jitterFactor);
```

marta: Also: cache idempotency keys in SDK with expiry adjusted by skew so retries from the same process reuse the key until safe. And record a telemetry event when server rejects as expired vs deduped so we can measure freq.

paul: I can own a patch to the sample app that demos server-backed idempotency and an e2e that simulates 429 + delayed processing. Will add notes in the onboarding doc about avoiding client-only TTLs.

alyssa: Perfect — thanks. I'll open an ISSUE with repro steps, logs, and request IDs.

jamie: I'll file an SDK ticket to implement skew adjustment + default jittered backoff and add a changelog entry.

marta: Assign tickets to the devex incubator and SDK teams, add labels: idempotency, skew, retry.

paul: PR incoming from me in ~2 days, will include test harness for delayed processing. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: test/deploy job completed for branch fix/idempotency-sample — status: success :white_check_mark:

alyssa: Nice. Follow-up: add note in quickstart that shows how to opt into server-backed tokens and links to the SDK helper.

jamie: Also add telemetry flag and dashboard to track TTL-mismatch occurrences so we can quantify.

marta: Cool — thanks everyone.

alyssa: Thanks — will update thread when ISSUE + PRs are up. :raised_hands:
